Who we are

Fighting Food Insecurity
from the Ground Up

Founded in 2019 by community activist Nandi Dlamini, Roots of Hope Foundation began as a single vegetable garden in Soweto. Today we operate a network of twelve gardens across Soweto, Alexandra, Tembisa, and Katlehong — serving thousands of families with fresh produce, skills training, and a stronger sense of community.

Our mission: to empower South African communities through sustainable urban farming, nutrition education, and food security programmes that create lasting change.

Our Story

From a single garden in Soweto to a network of twelve — growing food security and community across Gauteng.

How we began

Rooted in Community

Roots of Hope Foundation was founded in 2019 by community activist Nandi Dlamini in direct response to rising food insecurity affecting low-income families across Gauteng. Witnessing families in Soweto struggle to access fresh, nutritious food, Nandi transformed a vacant plot into the organisation's first community vegetable garden.

What began as a single garden with twelve volunteer families has since grown into a network of twelve gardens across four townships — Soweto, Alexandra, Tembisa, and Katlehong. Today, Roots of Hope serves over 3,000 beneficiaries annually, combining sustainable urban farming with nutrition education to create lasting change.

The organisation is registered as a non-profit in accordance with the South African Non-Profit Organisations Act 71 of 1997, supported by a growing network of corporate sponsors, individual donors, and community volunteers.

What drives us

Mission & Vision

Our Mission

To empower South African communities through sustainable urban farming, nutrition education, and food security programmes that create lasting change.

Our Vision

A food-secure South Africa where every community has access to fresh, nutritious food and the knowledge to cultivate it.

Our Programmes

From community vegetable gardens to youth leadership — discover how Roots of Hope is creating lasting change across Gauteng.

Programme 1

Urban Food Gardens

Our flagship programme operates twelve community vegetable gardens across Soweto, Alexandra, Tembisa, and Katlehong. Each garden is managed by trained community members and produces a diverse range of vegetables — including spinach, tomatoes, butternut, and sweet potato — available to beneficiary families throughout the growing season.

Garden participants receive:

  • Hands-on training in sustainable urban farming techniques
  • Regular access to fresh, organically grown produce
  • Seeds, tools, and equipment provided by the foundation
  • Monthly visits from agricultural advisors
Volunteer at a Garden
Programme 2

Nutrition Education

Every week, Roots of Hope facilitates nutrition education workshops at garden sites and community centres across all four townships. Led by trained health workers and dietitians, these sessions give families the knowledge they need to make informed choices about their diet.

Workshop topics include:

  • Understanding food groups and balanced meals
  • Budget-friendly cooking with fresh garden produce
  • Food preservation and seasonal eating
  • Nutrition for children aged 0–5 and pregnant mothers
Register for a Workshop
Programme 3

Youth Development

The Youth Development Programme engages young people aged 12–25 in sustainable agriculture, environmental education, and community leadership. Participants complete a structured 12-week curriculum combining practical garden work with classroom-based learning in entrepreneurship and environmental stewardship.

Programme outcomes include:

  • Certificate in Urban Farming and Food Security (NQF-aligned)
  • Leadership and project management skills
  • Community service hours recognised by partner schools
  • Mentorship from experienced agricultural professionals
